# Altair Vega Code for Seattle Weather Dataset

Here's a Python code example using Altair to visualize the Seattle weather dataset (seattle-weather.csv):

```python
import altair as alt
import pandas as pd

# Load the dataset
url = "https://raw.githubusercontent.com/vega/vega-datasets/main/data/seattle-weather.csv"
weather = pd.read_csv(url)

# Convert date to datetime format
weather['date'] = pd.to_datetime(weather['date'])

# Basic line chart of temperature over time
line_chart = alt.Chart(weather).mark_line().encode(
    x='date:T',
    y='temp_max:C',
    color='weather:N',
    tooltip=['date:T', 'temp_max:C', 'weather:N']
).properties(
    title='Seattle Maximum Temperature by Weather Type',
    width=600,
    height=400
)

# Bar chart of precipitation
bar_chart = alt.Chart(weather).mark_bar().encode(
    x='date:T',
    y='precipitation:Q',
    color='weather:N',
    tooltip=['date:T', 'precipitation:Q', 'weather:N']
).properties(
    title='Seattle Precipitation by Weather Type',
    width=600,
    height=400
)

# Weather distribution
weather_dist = alt.Chart(weather).mark_arc().encode(
    alt.Color('weather:N', legend=None),
    alt.Theta('count():Q')
).properties(
    title='Distribution of Weather Types in Seattle',
    width=400,
    height=400
)

# Display the charts
line_chart | bar_chart | weather_dist
```

## Alternative Visualizations

Here are a few more visualization options:

1. **Scatter plot of temperature vs precipitation:**
```python
scatter = alt.Chart(weather).mark_circle(size=60).encode(
    x='temp_max:Q',
    y='precipitation:Q',
    color='weather:N',
    tooltip=['date:T', 'temp_max:Q', 'precipitation:Q', 'weather:N']
).properties(
    title='Temperature vs Precipitation by Weather Type',
    width=500,
    height=400
)
```

2. **Monthly average temperature:**
```python
monthly_temp = alt.Chart(weather).mark_line(point=True).encode(
    x='month(date):O',
    y='mean(temp_max):Q',
    color='weather:N'
).properties(
    title='Monthly Average Maximum Temperature',
    width=500,
    height=400
)
```

3. **Weather type counts by month:**
```python
weather_by_month = alt.Chart(weather).mark_bar().encode(
    x='month(date):O',
    y='count():Q',
    color='weather:N',
    column='weather:N'
).properties(
    title='Weather Type Counts by Month',
    width=alt.Step(40)  # controls width of each subplot
)
```

To use this code, you'll need to have Altair and pandas installed:
```
pip install altair pandas vega_datasets
```
